To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the rotation function is a sensitive probe of similarity between protein structures; (2) high resolution data and high percentage identity of target and search molecules are the most important factors in the cross rotation function; (3) the rotation function peak heights for cross rotation functions are almost linearly related to a measure of the similarity between protein structures.

(i) the cross rotation function peak heights increase as the structural distance, between the search and target structures, decreases, (ii) the peak heights increase as resolution increases, and (iii) the peak heights are higher if the radius of integration is large.

the rotation function peak heights are a function of: (1) the percentage identity of the target and the search molecules; (2) the resolution of the data; (3) the radius of integration used; and (4) the structural distance between the target and the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new techniques for solving the phase problem in X-ray crystallography.
the development of a method to improve the success rate of molecular replacement using protein homologues.

developing a rotation function which will work for a wide range of target and search molecules, with the aim of making the rotation function a more reliable tool for solving the phases of unknown structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cross rotation function is a sensitive probe of the structural similarity between two proteins and that the magnitude of the cross rotation peaks is a measure of the similarity of the two molecules.
the more similar the target and search structures the better.
the cross rotation function peak height depends on the degree of structural similarity, the resolution of the F(obs) data and the radius of integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cross rotation function is a useful method of determining the orientation of a search model with respect to a target molecule, even when the percentage identities are as low as 30%.
a search model which is 70 80% identical with the target molecule should give good rotation function results for a target of high resolution (2.5 3.0 A) and a radius of integration of 25 30 A.
, in the case of homologous proteins, the rotation function can provide an estimate for the structural distance between the search and target molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross rotation function is a useful tool in molecular replacement.
the use of protein homologue models in the rotation function can significantly improve the quality of the rotation function solution.
the cross rotation function is sensitive to the similarity between target and search structures and that this sensitivity can be used to estimate the degree of structural homology between proteins.
